Review: The problem is well scoped as an apparatus-specific validation study. It distinguishes what the supplied scans show from what they cannot establish, and it avoids treating the two scans as independent repeats or combining their differently scaled DOP values. The proposed joint, randomized measurements address the central uncertainty: whether spread and mean phase provide repeatable control of DOP and polarization direction with acceptably low cross-coupling. Calibrated Stokes reconstruction, reference-state tracking, equivalence testing, and separate reporting of within-run and between-session variation are appropriate safeguards.

The system-level comparison is also feasible in principle: a fixed task, matched baseline, prespecified meaningful improvement, and pilot-based power planning make the performance claim testable. However, the study depends on access to the original SLM apparatus and a stable polarimetry setup; the supplied data do not establish that this access or the original phase-generation protocol is available. A single fixed classification task supports only an apparatus-and-task-specific conclusion. Also, equivalence conclusions will depend on defensible task-derived margins and adequate repeated measurements across the operating range; neither can be finalized from these scans alone. Novelty remains uncertain pending a targeted literature review.

Feedback: Before data collection, specify the operating ranges and grid resolution, define how polarization-direction error will be quantified, and state the task-derived equivalence margins and minimum meaningful performance gain. Verify the `dphi` units and phase-generation procedure against source documentation, and confirm apparatus access. Use pilot data to estimate drift and measurement noise, then power the study for both the equivalence tests and the system-level comparison. If the original apparatus cannot be accessed, frame any substitute as a replication or extension on a different system, not validation of the original apparatus.

Rating (1-5): 4
